newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp preparing for single Euro currency.
newsitem.headline: Krupp preparing for single Euro currency.

text.p: German steel and engineering group Krupp said on Wednesday it is actively preparing for the start of the single European currency, and that it sees the advantages outweighing the disadvantages.

"The opportunities offered by the euro unambiguously outweigh the indisputable risks," said Gerhard Cromme, chairman of Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp, in remarks prepared for delivery at the company's annual news conference.
"Krupp therefore favours the timely and rapid introduction of currency union."

Krupp is already intensively preparing for the start of European monetary union (EMU), which is scheduled for January 1999. Working groups are planning the coordination and implementation of the conversion throughout the company, Cromme said.

About 70 percent of Krupp's sales are within the European Union. Currency union will increase market transparency and eliminate exchange risk among European currencies, allowing more exact planning, Cromme said.
Transaction and hedging costs will also be sharply reduced, and the company will have access to a much broader capital market, he said.
